subject: Functions for use with and without Shiny

messages.subject: Functions for use with and without Shiny
parts:
Hello -
has anybody found an elegant way to make Shiny functions in server.R usable also without Shiny (meaning as normal R functions)? I essentially end up duplicating all reactive functions and have a hard time always making changes to both versions (with and without Shiny). 
Thanks,
D.

messages.author: 2b46f14139c84304
messages.subject: Re: Functions for use with and without Shiny
parts:
For the example on http://shiny.rstudio.com :

myPlot <- function(n_breaks, bw_adjust, individual_obs, density) {
  hist(faithful$eruptions,
       probability = TRUE,
       breaks = as.numeric(n_breaks),
       xlab = "Duration (minutes)",
       main = "Geyser eruption duration")
 
  if (individual_obs) {
    rug(faithful$eruptions)
  }
 
  if (density) {
    dens <- density(faithful$eruptions,
                    adjust = bw_adjust)
    lines(dens, col = "blue")
  }
}

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
 
  output$main_plot <- renderPlot({
    myPlot(input$n_breaks,  input$bw_adjust, input$individual_obs, input$density)
  })
})

On 24.08.2014 11:35, Sigbert Klinke wrote:
> For the example on http://shiny.rstudio.com :
>

> […]

TBH, this solution only partially solves the problem. In case when you
have a "network" of reactives, you'd need to repeat all the wiring
between reactives and outputs manually, e.g.:


#v+
alpha <- function(foo, bar) { … }
beta <- function(alpha, foo) { … }
gamma <- function(alpha, beta) { … }
plot1 <- function(alpha, beta) { … }
plot2 <- function(alpha, gamma) { … }

#--- standalone
standalonePlot1 <- function(foo, bar) {
plot1(alpha(foo, bar), beta(alpha(foo, bar), foo))
}

standalonePlot2 <- function(foo, bar) {
plot2(alpha(foo, bar), gamma(alpha(foo, bar), beta(alpha(foo, bar),
foo))))
}

#--- shiny
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
rAlpha <- reactive({ alpha(input$foo, input$bar) })
rBeta <- reactive({ beta(rAlpha, input$foo) })
rGamma <- reactive({ gamma(rAlpha, rBeta) })

output$plot1 <- renderPlot({ plot1(rAlpha, rBeta) })
output$plot2 <- renderPlot({ plot2(rAlpha, rGamma) })
})
#v-


You can see that the `standalone` and `shiny` parts basically duplicate
the description of dependencies of each item, leading to DRY violation.

Is there a method of having this network usable also without invoking
the full web interface?


--
Tomasz Melcer
